ranking.note: placed after its prerequisites (36520, 29409) since neither can sit below the PR they unblock; still the category-defining milestone
raised to P2 for consistency with 36105: both fix the bitcoin wrapper being outright unusable for a class of users (packaged installs vs Windows)

inconsistencies: Overlap: #32387 (ipc windows support) states it also fixes the Windows wrapper binary to track child exit statuses, which is exactly the content of #36105. #36105 looks like that fix split out for separate review; review #36105 first and rebase/strip the duplicate commit from #32387.

Dependency chain, review in this order: #36520 (crash hardening) -> #29409 (expose Chain over IPC) -> #10102 (multiprocess milestone) -> #19460 (bitcoin-wallet -ipcconnect) -> #19461 (bitcoin-gui -ipcconnect). #19461 contains a single unique commit on top of the rest, so it is only reviewable after the others.
#36190 (Windows wrapper exit-status tests) tests the behaviour introduced by #36105; it is only meaningful once #36105 (or the equivalent commit in #32387) is settled.

#35932 and #36097 both carry temporary libmultiprocess subtree commits (upstream #335 and #342); their subtree bumps and #32387's libmultiprocess update will need sequencing to avoid conflicting subtree states.

#33117 and #36097 both extend node-facing interfaces for external consumers but at very different levels: #36097 changes IPC call mechanics (cancellation semantics agreed in RFC #33575) while #33117 adds a method set with GUI consumers waiting; both land in P2 but #36097 is the one whose semantics are hard to change later.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: four P1s are either live crash fixes in shipped multiprocess functionality (#35932, #36520) or the Chain-exposure/process-separation chain itself (#29409, #10102). P2 covers platform coverage and wrapper usability plus the per-executable -ipcconnect work; P3 is test/build hardening with no user-visible consequence. Only one band change was needed (#36106).
